name: Low Pay Commission — minimum wage coverage and bite (Report 2025 data annexes)

model.name: LPC analysis of the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE)
model.method: Coverage is the number and share of employee JOBS paid at or below the applicable NMW/NLW rate, measured from ASHE's April reference-period hourly pay excluding overtime. Bite is the applicable rate as a percentage of the ASHE median hourly wage of full-time workers. First-year apprentices are excluded from 2013 onwards.
model.method_basis: Low Pay Commission Report 2025, sources and notes to the data annexes

unit_note: Coverage counts JOBS, which is a unit concept this repo did not previously have. One person can hold two jobs and one household several, so a job count is never interchangeable with persons, households, benefit units or families — uk_aliases records lpc:jobs DISTINCT from dwp_hbai:persons and uk_hmrc:individuals.
period: ASHE April reference years, carried as calendar years. The regional coverage table is April 2025.
geographies: UK plus the twelve ITL-1 regions and nations, using the repo's registered UK region names (LPC prints 'East of England' where the rest of the repo says 'East'; aliased once).
coverage_note: What is READ: main annex sheets 5.2 (bite and coverage of the adult rate, UK, 1999-2025) and 6.7 right (bite by age band, UK, 2013-2025), plus the coverage annex's 'Region and nation' table. What is deliberately NOT read, and tallied by the build: 191 of the 193 main-annex sheets (the report's other figures — earnings distributions, employment effects, international comparisons — each its own population decision), and the 349-row local-authority coverage table.
local_authority_note: Local-authority geography is finer than any UK geography this repo registers, and the certified policyengine-uk world cannot resolve it either. Opening an LA vocabulary for one table would create identities nothing else can join to, so the table is a declared drop with a tallied row count rather than an omission.
diagnosis_upstream: BITE IS A DIFFERENT-DATA COMPARISON BEFORE IT IS ANYTHING ELSE. Its denominator is ASHE's median hourly wage of full-time workers; ASHE is an employer survey of jobs and PE-UK's certified world is FRS-based, a household survey, whose hourly-pay distribution is not ASHE's. Every bite claim carries that denominator in conditions, and the survey-population axis must be sized before any engine defect is named — and then only through the citable-known-issue gate. Underpayment (jobs paid BELOW the rate through non-compliance) is a compliance quantity with no PE-UK counterpart and is not staged here at all.
